title: Unbeaten India and Sri Lanka Clash for Women's T20 Asia Cup Glory
summary:
Two unbeaten teams. One trophy. On Sunday, India and Sri Lanka meet in the Women's T20 Asia Cup final at Dubai International Stadium, with India chasing a record-extending eighth title and Sri Lanka determined to defend the crown they won two years ago.

India are heavy favorites. They have won seven Women's Asia Cup titles — the most of any team — and have reached the final in every edition they've played. Their opening pair, Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana, are the tournament's top two run-scorers, with 168 and 154 runs respectively. Shafali has two half-centuries, including identical 64s against Thailand and Bangladesh. Mandhana blasted 124 against Hong Kong. With the ball, all-rounder Deepti Sharma has been dominant, taking 11 wickets at an average of just 3.63.

But Sri Lanka have their own weapon: captain Chamari Athapaththu. The right-arm off-break bowler also has 11 wickets, tied with Deepti for the tournament lead. Left-arm spinner Sugandika Kumari has added six more. And Sri Lanka know how to beat India in a final — they did it in 2024, winning by eight wickets.

India reached the final by defeating Bangladesh by 40 runs on Thursday. Sri Lanka edged Pakistan by four wickets in a low-scoring thriller on Friday. In their last T20 meeting, in December 2025, India won by 15 runs to sweep the series 5-0. India have also won nine of their last 10 T20 internationals against Sri Lanka.

History and form point to India. But finals have a way of surprising everyone. The match begins at 6:30 p.m. local time (14:30 GMT).
why_it_matters: Women's cricket is one of the fastest-growing sports in the world, and results in tournaments like this one shape the sponsorship, broadcast deals and professional leagues that decide whether the next generation of girls can build a career out of the game.

background_read: Cricket is the biggest sport in both India and Sri Lanka, and the Asia Cup is a regional tournament organised by the Asian Cricket Council, with the women's T20 version long dominated by India. The final is being staged at Dubai International Stadium, a ground in the United Arab Emirates — a neutral Gulf country that hosts many Asian tournaments because teams such as India and Pakistan do not play each other at home for political reasons.

The T20 format, 20 overs a side and finished in about three hours, has driven the women's game's rapid growth. India launched the Women's Premier League in 2023, the first big-money franchise league for women cricketers, giving stars such as Smriti Mandhana (India's opening batter and one of the sport's best-known names) full-time professional contracts.

Sri Lanka's 2024 title, won by beating India by eight wickets in the final, was their first in the competition and turned captain Chamari Athapaththu (a Sri Lankan all-rounder who has played in overseas franchise leagues) into one of the country's most recognisable athletes.

perspectives.perspective: Positive — India's supporters and the game's promoters
perspectives.description: India's dominance — seven titles, the tournament's two leading run-scorers and its joint-best bowler — shows what a well-funded domestic system can produce. An eighth crown would strengthen the argument for more investment in women's cricket across Asia and beyond.

The gap between India and the smaller teams keeps widening, and a one-sided final would underline how uneven the funding is across the region. Critics also point out that women's prize money, salaries and broadcast exposure still lag far behind the men's Asia Cup.

Sri Lanka's 2024 win is a reminder that finals are rarely decided by form alone, and the growth of franchise leagues has begun to spread top-level experience beyond the traditional powers. That pattern tends to make regional tournaments tighter and less predictable over time.

Whatever happens on Sunday, the result will influence selection, confidence and funding going into the next global women's tournament. Both boards will also be watching how many new fans a close, well-attended final attracts.
